text: Joe Powell (21 March 1922 – 30 June 2016) was an English stuntman and actor, widely recognized as the "daddy of British stuntmen." Born in Shepherd's Bush, London, he joined the British Army and served in the 1st Battalion Royal Fusiliers Cadet Corps. He enjoyed soldiering and, at the age of 17, shortly after the outbreak of the Second World War, joined the Grenadier Guards. To escape the monotony of drill and physical training, he began boxing with the regimental team; however, as the war progressed, he was selected for No 4 Special Service (Commando) unit, participating in the 1942 raid on Dieppe, during which he was briefly knocked out, and in the D-Day invasion. In 1946, he met actor Dennis Price, which led to him securing a role as an extra at Pinewood Studios. While sparring at London's Polytechnic Boxing Club, he became a founding partner in a stunt team with Captain Jock Easton. Powell performed stuntwork in numerous films, including The Guns of Navarone (1961), The Longest Day (1962), Cleopatra (1963), Zulu (1964), Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines (1965), and The Man Who Would Be King (1975), and also took part in several James Bond films. He is listed by The Guardian as having performed one of the ten-best film stunts ever. Powell was twice married, first to Marguerite and later to Juliet, and was survived by four sons and a daughter. He was the brother of Eddie Powell, who was also a film stuntman. Powell authored a book about his life titled The Life and Times of a Fall Guy. This article about an English film actor is a stub.
